source.title: Adaptive Early-Learning Correction for Segmentation from Noisy Annotations
source.authors: Sheng Liu; Kangning Liu; Weicheng Zhu; Yiqiu Shen; C. Fernandez-Granda

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix text are present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: Reports early learning followed by memorization in segmentation networks trained on noisy annotations, extending the behavior to medical segmentation and weakly supervised semantic segmentation.
record.gate_note: The study measures learning curves on incorrectly annotated pixels and reports their behavior. Results cited from classification papers are not counted as this study’s results. The curve values are presented in figures; the text describes their trends but does not give exact values.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures early learning and subsequent memorization on incorrectly annotated training pixels, extending V6 to medical and weakly supervised semantic segmentation. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: segmentation networks exhibit early learning followed by memorization with category-dependent timing, and ADELE exploits this behavior to correct annotations and improve segmentation. Add that poor initial annotations and highly structured noise can undermine this approach and may prevent early learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains segmentation models on pixel-wise noisy annotations and measures IoU on incorrectly labeled pixels over epochs. Noise is synthetic human-like dilation/erosion for SegTHOR and classification-model-generated annotations for PASCAL VOC; it does not use completely random image labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning and memorization occur at different speeds across semantic categories. The paper also reports that highly structured annotation noise may prevent early learning and that ADELE's effect depends on initial annotation quality.

fits_no_version.finding: ADELE suppresses agreement with erroneous annotations and sustains ground-truth learning by correcting labels and enforcing multiscale consistency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive annotation correction and multiscale consistency can mitigate memorization in segmentation trained with noisy annotations.

record.problems: The early-learning and memorization curves are plotted without exact values or uncertainty estimates. The tested noise is not completely random labeling: it is synthetic dilation/erosion or weakly supervised annotations. The study reports category-dependent timing and notes that highly structured noise may prevent early learning.
record.rows_left_out: None. The paper also reports segmentation-performance comparisons and ablations for ADELE, but those outcomes do not directly measure the early-learning/memorization behavior specified by V6.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across a clean-to-completely-random label sweep. The morphological-noise severity sweep does not establish these properties.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
Completely random labels and a controlled comparison of separate real-label and random-label training runs; the direct evidence concerns partially incorrect segmentation annotations.

missing.what: Qualitative examples and the explicit argument that highly structured, repeated annotation errors may prevent early learning. Record the tentative wording rather than coding proven absence.
missing.locator: Section 6; Figure 18; Appendix A.1, Highly structured annotation noise

record.verdict_notes: Exact curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text, but captions and prose explicitly describe the baseline trajectories. ADELE's mitigation results should not receive a V6 limits_scope verdict merely because the intervention changes those trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, chance test error, and fitting without changes to architecture or training hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time for random labels versus true labels, and convergence rate as corruption increases, are not tested.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The study does not sweep from clean to fully random labels or report training error and test error across that sweep.
The study does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or their necessity for generalization.

Tests early learning and later memorization in segmentation with noisy annotations, including labels generated for weakly supervised segmentation. It does not test classification models or completely random labels.
